instructions: Fill a medium pot with water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Set a large bowl of ice water next to the stove.
Meanwhile, cut the squid bodies into rings about 1/2 inch wide and cut any tentacles in half.
Finely mince the garlic and transfer it to a large bowl. Add the sugar and mash the two together with the back of a spoon until it looks like wet sand.
Squeeze in the juice of the lime and add the fish sauce. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

In a second bowl, combine 2 thinly sliced celery stalks, half the red onion sliced thin, the green onions sliced, the carrot cut into thin matchsticks, the tomato cut into thin wedges and the cilantro, chopped.
Slice the chilies and put them in a small bowl for the table.
Add the squid to the boiling water and cook for 1 minute, until the rings turn opaque and curl. Don't leave it longer or it turns rubbery.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the squid to the ice water for 1 minute, then drain it well.
Add the squid to the dressing and toss. Add the vegetables and herbs and toss again.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more sugar or a splash of fish sauce.
Serve right away, with the sliced chilies on the side.
method_notes: Hungry in Thailand and Cup of Yum give the same dish: squid blanched for about 30 seconds, then tossed in a dressing of crushed garlic and chilies, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar, with celery, onion, tomato, carrot and cilantro. Hungry in Thailand (5 out of 5 from 1 vote, so below the 20 ratings needed) uses more sugar, Cup of Yum less; this lands in between, doubled for 4. The chilies move to the table so the base stays mild.
